source.paper: Card, D. (1995). Using Geographic Variation in College Proximity to Estimate the Return to Schooling. In L. N. Christofides, E. K. Grant and R. Swidinsky (eds.), Aspects of Labour Market Behaviour: Essays in Honour of John Vanderkamp, University of Toronto Press, 201-222. Same tables as NBER Working Paper 4832 (1994).
source.table: Table 3, Panel A ('Treat experience and experience squared as exogenous'), no family-background controls: row 2 column (5) for the 2SLS return to education; row 1 column (1) for the first stage; row 1 column (3) for the reduced form. Notes: sample size 3010; controls are a black indicator, southern and SMSA residence in 1976, region dummies and SMSA residence in 1966, experience and experience squared. Read from the page image of the author-hosted copy https://davidcard.berkeley.edu/papers/geo_var_schooling.pdf (PDF page 35) on 2026-11-19.
source.data_check: proximity.zip nls.dat has 3,613 rows; 3,010 have a valid 1976 log wage, matching the Table 3 sample size. A 2SLS fit on the public file with exper = age76 - ed76 - 6 and the controls above gave 0.1315 (SE 0.0550), first stage 0.3199 (checked 2026-11-19).

pass_if: The replicated 2SLS return is within 0.005 of 0.132 and the first-stage coefficient within 0.005 of 0.320 (rounding only; the public file reproduces both to three decimals).
The paper states the published numbers it compares against, citing Table 3.
